scenarios.title: Respect
scenarios.text: After his first home match in Japan, the squad lines up and bows to the fans. Then the fans bow back. Then they clean their section of the stadium. He has never seen anything like it.

choices.label: Join in properly
choices.text: He bows deeper than anyone and stays behind to help the kit staff. The fans notice. A local paper writes about the foreigner who cleaned the dressing room.

choices.label: Watch and learn first
choices.text: He watches and asks questions. A teammate explains everything over ramen. Respect, slowly earned.

scenarios.title: The Pagode
scenarios.text: In the Brazilian dressing room, before every match: drums, singing, dancing, a pagode band made of kit bags and water bottles. Everyone is expected to join in. Even the goalkeeping coach.

choices.label: Dance like nobody's watching
choices.text: He dances terribly and with total commitment. The squad goes wild. He's one of them now.

choices.label: Learn a drum
choices.text: A teammate teaches him the pandeiro. By the end of the season, he's the band's best player.

scenarios.title: Tuesday Night in the Rain
scenarios.text: A Tuesday night in the north of England. Horizontal rain, four degrees, a pitch like a swamp. A local teammate looks at his face and laughs: 'Welcome to football, mate.'

choices.label: Embrace it
choices.hint: The fans will love it. Your fingers won't.
choices.text: Short sleeves, no gloves, total commitment. The fans adopt him. He can't feel his hands until Thursday.

choices.label: Gloves, tights, snood, everything
choices.text: Gloves, tights, a snood. The away fans sing a song about his snood. He's warm. He doesn't care.

scenarios.title: A Different Rhythm
scenarios.text: Training at 9pm because of the heat. Matches at midnight. Weekends on different days. A compound with pools, palm trees and other foreign players. It's comfortable and very strange.

choices.label: Explore beyond the compound
choices.desc: The desert, the markets, the people.
choices.text: He goes into the desert with a teammate's family and eats under the stars. The country becomes real to him.

choices.label: Focus on football and savings
choices.text: Training, recovery, savings. A quiet, profitable chapter.

scenarios.title: Military Service
scenarios.text: Every Korean man must do military service before he's twenty-eight, unless he wins something big for the country. His time is running out.

choices.label: Serve with the army football club
choices.desc: Two seasons in the army team.
choices.text: He joins the army club. Shaved head, early mornings, lower league. He comes out more disciplined than ever.

choices.label: Chase an exemption with the national team
choices.desc: Win a medal, serve your country that way.
choices.text: Everything rides on the next tournament with the national team. No pressure.

scenarios.title: The Bicycle
scenarios.text: His Dutch teammates cycle to training. In the rain. The captain, a millionaire, arrives on a bike with a child seat on the back. {J} is still driving.

choices.label: Buy a bike
choices.text: He buys a bike and falls off it twice in the first week. By spring he cycles to training like a local. The squad is delighted.

choices.label: Keep driving
choices.text: He keeps driving. The squad calls him 'the taxi'.

scenarios.title: Ketchup
scenarios.text: At the team dinner, he puts ketchup on his pasta. The table goes silent. An Italian teammate puts down his fork and looks at him like he's committed a crime.

choices.label: Apologise and ask to be taught
choices.text: Three teammates take him to a nonna's kitchen for a 'pasta education'. He gains two kilos and a family.

choices.label: Add more ketchup
choices.text: He adds more. The table explodes in mock outrage. It becomes a legendary dressing-room joke.

scenarios.title: Dinner at Eleven
scenarios.text: His teammates have invited him to dinner. At 11pm. On a Tuesday. He's usually asleep by ten.

choices.label: Go, and adapt
choices.text: Dinner until 1am, laughing, talking, tapas. He's exhausted at training and completely part of the group.

choices.label: Go for an hour
choices.text: He goes for an hour, leaves at midnight, and is teased for being 'the grandfather'.

scenarios.title: Christmas Alone
scenarios.text: The squad is going home to families for a couple of days. {J}'s family is thousands of kilometres away. A teammate notices him planning to spend it alone.

choices.label: Accept the teammate's invitation
choices.text: A loud family dinner in a language he half understands. The grandmother gives him a scarf she knitted. He'll keep it forever.

choices.label: Video call home all day
choices.text: Twelve hours of video calls with family. Tiring, lovely.

scenarios.title: Lunar New Year
scenarios.text: The club is hosting a Lunar New Year event: lion dances, red envelopes for the kids, and a tradition where a player has to feed a lion an orange. They've chosen {J}.

choices.label: Feed the lion with style
choices.text: He feeds the lion with great ceremony. The lion dances wildly. The crowd loves it. Good luck guaranteed for the season, apparently.

choices.label: Give out red envelopes to the kids
choices.text: He hands out red envelopes to a hundred kids. He runs out and has to borrow money from the president.

scenarios.title: Supporters' Culture
scenarios.text: The supporters' group has invited him to their base: a small building covered in murals, drums, flags and photographs of legends. They want him to sign the wall.

choices.label: Go, sign the wall, stay for tea
choices.text: He signs the wall next to the legends and stays for tea and stories until midnight. From now on, he's theirs.

choices.label: Send a signed shirt
choices.text: He sends a signed shirt. It's framed. The fans would have preferred him.

scenarios.title: Dreaming in Another Language
scenarios.text: He wakes up and realises he dreamed in the local language. A full dream. Including an argument with the referee.

choices.label: Give your next interview in the language
choices.text: His interview is nearly perfect. One mistake makes everyone smile. The fans see him as one of their own.

choices.label: Tell nobody, just enjoy it
choices.text: He smiles all day and doesn't tell anyone why.

scenarios.title: The Flat
scenarios.text: A landlord takes one look at him and suddenly the flat 'has been rented'. Ten minutes later, his white teammate calls about the same flat and it's available.
scenarios.prompt: Discrimination when looking for a home.

choices.label: Speak about it publicly
choices.text: His post about it starts a national conversation. The landlord apologises publicly. Other foreigners share their stories.

choices.label: Let the club handle it quietly
choices.text: The club finds him a better flat. The landlord is quietly blacklisted by every club in the city.

scenarios.title: The Local Delicacy
scenarios.text: His teammates have brought him the region's most famous delicacy. It smells extraordinary. It moves slightly. Everyone is filming.

out.text: He eats it all and asks for more. The squad is in awe. It's actually delicious.
He eats it all, smiling, then spends the evening in the bathroom. Legend status, all the same.

choices.label: One polite bite
choices.text: One bite. Polite applause. The squad is a little disappointed.

scenarios.title: The Village Festival
scenarios.text: His parents' village is holding its annual festival. They've asked him to be the guest of honour and to judge the cooking competition. Every grandmother in the village has entered.

choices.label: Judge honestly
choices.text: He picks a winner. Nine grandmothers are furious. One is ecstatic. {MUM} says he chose correctly.

choices.label: Declare a nine-way tie
choices.text: A nine-way tie. Every grandmother wins. He eats nine dishes and can't move.

scenarios.title: A Three-Day Wedding
scenarios.text: {T} has invited him to his wedding back home: three days of ceremonies, a thousand guests, traditions he doesn't understand, and a request that he wear the traditional outfit.
scenarios.prompt: Go to a teammate's traditional wedding?

choices.label: Go, outfit and all
choices.text: He wears the outfit, learns the dance and gets very emotional at a ceremony he doesn't understand. {T}'s family adopts him.

choices.label: Go for one day
choices.text: He attends the main day in a borrowed outfit. {T} is touched that he came.

scenarios.title: Fasting and Football
scenarios.text: A match during Ramadan, kick-off before sunset. He's been fasting all day. The club doctor has a plan: a drink at the exact moment of sunset, if play stops.

choices.label: Fast and play
choices.text: At sunset, the referee stops play for thirty seconds. Players from both teams break their fast on the touchline together. It's one of the most beautiful moments of his career.

choices.label: Make up the fast another day
choices.desc: Allowed for travellers and athletes, some say.
choices.text: He makes it up later in the month, after talking to his imam. Peace of mind.

scenarios.title: The Wrong Gift
scenarios.text: He brought a gift from home for the president's wife. Her face changes when she opens it. A teammate whispers that, here, that particular gift means something unlucky.

choices.label: Apologise sincerely and explain
choices.text: He explains the meaning back home. She laughs, relieved, and tells him the meaning here. Now they have a story.

choices.label: Send a second, better gift
choices.text: A second gift, researched carefully, arrives the next day. The president mentions it at the next board meeting, warmly.

scenarios.title: In His Language
scenarios.text: At the home match, the stands unfurl a banner written in his native language. It's slightly misspelled. It's the most beautiful thing he's ever seen.
scenarios.prompt: The fans wrote a banner in your language.

choices.label: Run to the stand at the end
choices.text: He runs to the stand and bows. The photo goes viral back home. {MUM} cries.

choices.label: Post a thank-you correcting the spelling, gently
choices.text: He posts the banner with the correct spelling and three hearts. The fans laugh and fix it for the next match.

scenarios.title: A Taste of Home
scenarios.text: He hasn't eaten food from home in four months. A teammate tells him there's a tiny restaurant on the other side of the city run by a family from his country.

choices.label: Go immediately
choices.text: The family recognises him and cries. He eats three plates. They refuse payment. He comes back every week for the rest of his time there.

choices.label: Bring the whole squad
choices.text: Twenty-five footballers in a tiny restaurant. The family makes a year's profit in a night. The squad discovers his food.

scenarios.title: Batik Day
scenarios.text: It's national batik day back home. Every Indonesian online is posting in batik. He's being tagged by thousands of fans asking where his post is.
scenarios.prompt: Wear batik for national batik day?

choices.label: Wear it to training
choices.text: He wears batik to training. His teammates ask a hundred questions. Three of them order shirts.

choices.label: Post a photo from home
choices.text: A photo with his whole family in matching batik. Millions of likes back home.

scenarios.title: Carnival
scenarios.text: It's Carnival. The whole city is dancing. The club has a strict rule: no Carnival parties for players during the season. Half the squad is planning to break it.

choices.label: Watch one parade, then home
choices.text: He watches one parade from a balcony, then goes home. It's the most colourful thing he's ever seen.

out.text: Nobody recognises him under the feathers. Best night of his life. Hard training on Monday.
The feathers fall off at 2am. A fan films him. The club fines him heavily.

scenarios.title: La Bombonera Energy
scenarios.text: Before his first home match, the stadium is shaking: literally, physically shaking. A teammate tells him the stands bounce when the fans jump. 'Don't be scared. It means they love you.'

choices.label: Jump with them in the warm-up
choices.text: He jumps with the crowd during the warm-up. They notice. They never stop singing for him.

choices.label: Focus on your game
choices.text: He focuses. A good performance wins them over more slowly.

scenarios.title: The Blessing
scenarios.text: Before the season, the club invites monks to bless the stadium, the players and the pitch. The ceremony is long, beautiful and in a language he doesn't know.

choices.label: Take it seriously
choices.text: He sits quietly through the whole ceremony and receives the white string on his wrist. A strange calm stays with him all week.

choices.label: Ask a teammate to explain everything
choices.text: His teammate explains every part. He learns something about the country, and about patience.

scenarios.title: Tailgate
scenarios.text: American football culture: three hours before kick-off, the car park is full of barbecues, music and families. Fans invite him to try a hot dog, which is against his diet plan.

choices.label: Walk through the tailgate and say hi
choices.text: He walks through the car park shaking hands. Thirty selfies, two hot dogs, a life-long fanbase.

choices.label: Wave from the bus
choices.text: He waves from the bus. They cheer anyway. Very friendly people.

scenarios.title: Two Minutes Late
scenarios.text: He arrives at the team meeting two minutes late. Back home, two minutes is early. Here, the whole room turns to look at him. There's a fine, and a look from the manager he won't forget.

choices.label: Never be late again
choices.text: From then on he's ten minutes early to everything. The manager notices. So does his family, back home, who are amazed.

choices.label: Joke about 'rubber time' at home
choices.text: He explains the concept of 'rubber time'. The squad laughs. The fine still applies.

scenarios.title: Tea, Constantly
scenarios.text: In Turkey, tea arrives every twenty minutes: in the dressing room, at the physio, during contract talks. He's drinking twelve glasses a day. The doctor is concerned.

choices.label: Embrace it
choices.text: Tea with everyone, every time. The kit man, the president, the groundsman. He knows everyone now.

choices.label: Switch to herbal tea
choices.text: He switches to herbal tea. The tea man is suspicious but accepts it.

scenarios.title: The Traffic
scenarios.text: Ten thousand motorbikes at every crossroads, in every direction at once. A teammate tells him the secret to crossing the road: walk slowly and never stop.

choices.label: Walk slowly and never stop
choices.text: He walks slowly into the river of motorbikes. They flow around him like water. He reaches the other side, alive and exhilarated.

choices.label: Take a taxi across the street
choices.text: He takes a taxi forty metres. The driver laughs the whole way. So do his teammates.

scenarios.title: Fika
scenarios.text: Every afternoon, the whole club stops for coffee and cake together: players, staff, cleaners, the president. Nobody talks about football. It's called fika.

choices.label: Embrace fika completely
choices.text: He starts looking forward to it more than training. He learns the names of everyone at the club, including the cleaner's grandchildren.

choices.label: Bring cake from home
choices.text: He brings a cake from home. It's gone in four minutes. He's asked to bring it every week.

scenarios.title: Yiayia
scenarios.text: His landlady is an eighty-year-old widow who has decided he's too thin. Food appears outside his door every day. She doesn't speak a word of his language.

choices.label: Learn to say thank you in Greek and visit
choices.text: He visits with flowers and his twelve words of Greek. She cries, feeds him more, and comes to every home match after that.

choices.label: Accept the food gratefully
choices.text: He eats everything. He gains a kilo and a grandmother.

scenarios.title: Day of the Dead
scenarios.text: A teammate invites him to his family's Day of the Dead celebration: an altar with photos of loved ones, marigolds, candles, food for the dead. He's asked if he wants to add a photo of someone he's lost.

choices.label: Add a photo of someone you lost
choices.text: He adds a photo of his grandmother. The family lights a candle for her. He cries, and feels lighter afterwards.

choices.label: Just observe respectfully
choices.text: He watches and listens. It changes how he thinks about grief.

scenarios.title: The Beach
scenarios.text: Recovery session on the beach. The coach says 'watch out for the rips'. A teammate says 'watch out for the sharks'. Another says 'watch out for the sun'. Nobody is joking.

choices.label: Stay between the flags
choices.text: He stays between the flags and learns to bodysurf. Best recovery session of his life.

choices.label: Try surfing
choices.text: He tries surfing, falls off forty times and stands up once. The squad films the once.
